nodes.content: Develop semantic parsers that generalize to unseen operator compositions despite training correlations between linguistic templates and program structure.
requirements: Achieve 80% exact-match accuracy on held-out operator compositions under reversed template–structure correlations.
Retain in-distribution exact-match accuracy within two percentage points of an identically sized, conventionally trained parser.

nodes.content: Train SwapParse using operator-aligned counterfactual template swaps and compositional decoding, with in-distribution distillation from a same-size baseline.
What fraction of SwapParse template swaps preserve operator scope in nested negation–quantifier utterances?
At least 95% of operator-aligned SwapParse template swaps preserve gold scope on nested negation–quantifier utterances.
Blindly annotate operator scope for 400 nested negation–quantifier SwapParse swaps; compare with source programs to measure preservation.
Blind annotation found 386 of 400 SwapParse swaps (96.5%) preserved gold negation–quantifier scope.
Proceed with operator-aligned SwapParse swaps, filtering scope-ambiguous samples because audited preservation reached 96.5%.
Filter scope-ambiguous swaps, then audit 200 swaps per negation–quantifier ordering and report post-filter gold-scope preservation.
Apply scope-ambiguity filters to SwapParse swaps and blindly annotate 200 retained examples for each negation–quantifier ordering.
SwapParse ScopeAudit-v1: 400 retained swaps with blind scope labels, ordering strata, filter decisions, and preservation-rate calculations.
Reannotate 80 stratified ScopeAudit-v1 swaps; compare scope labels and independently verify per-ordering preservation calculations.
ScopeAudit-v1 reannotation agreed on 78/80 labels; verified gold-scope preservation was 198/200 and 197/200 by ordering.
Train same-size SwapParse and conventional parsers on TemplateFlip-v1; measure reversed-correlation held-out composition and in-distribution exact match across five seeds.
Across five TemplateFlip-v1 seeds, SwapParse scored 76.8% held-out exact match, below 80%; in-distribution accuracy trailed baseline by 1.3 points.
Keep audited swaps and distillation, but revise compositional decoding to address 76.8% held-out accuracy while preserving in-distribution performance.
Retain filtered swaps and distillation; audit scope preservation in 400 new nested cases, then add scope-constrained decoding.
Annotate 400 new nested swaps for scope preservation, then implement scope-constrained decoding using audited operator-order constraints.
ScopeAudit-v2 extends v1 with 400 additional nested-swap scope labels, machine-readable operator-order constraints, and a scope-constrained decoder.
Independently reannotate 80 ScopeAudit-v2 swaps, verify decoding constraints, and rerun five-seed TemplateFlip-v1 held-out and in-distribution exact-match comparisons.
ScopeAudit-v2 preserved gold scope in 390/400 new swaps (97.5%); independent reannotation agreed on 79/80 labels.
Train TypeBind with typed operator-slot supervision, template-adversarial structural embeddings, and baseline-logit anchoring for in-distribution fidelity.
Does TypeBind's template adversary reduce template-ID probe accuracy below 30% while retaining at least 95% operator-slot labeling accuracy?
With adversarial weight 0.2, TypeBind achieves under 30% template-ID probe accuracy and at least 95% operator-slot labeling accuracy.
Train TypeBind at adversarial weight 0.2 across five TemplateFlip-v1 seeds; measure template-ID probe, slot accuracy, and both exact-match splits.
TypeBind averaged 26% template-ID probe accuracy, 96% operator-slot accuracy, 82% held-out exact match, and a 1.2-point in-distribution deficit.
Ablate TypeBind's adversary and slot supervision separately across five TemplateFlip-v1 seeds; compare template-ID probes and both exact-match splits.
On TemplateFlip-v1 triple-operator held-outs, TypeBind reached 73% exact match versus 84% without its adversary, missing the 80% target.
Keep TypeBind's slot supervision and anchoring; disable adversarial loss for triple operators, where full TypeBind scored 73%.
Does triple-operator-only adversary removal recover exact match while keeping TypeBind's overall template-ID probe below 30%?
TypeBind without triple-operator adversarial loss achieves at least 80% triple-operator exact match and under 30% overall template-ID probe accuracy.
Train triple-operator-gated TypeBind across five TemplateFlip-v1 seeds; evaluate triple-operator exact match and overall template-ID probe accuracy.
Triple-operator-gated TypeBind averaged 83% triple-operator exact match and 28% overall template-ID probe accuracy across five seeds.
Evaluate frozen gated TypeBind on TemplateFlip-v1's held-out triple compositions, reporting per-family exact match and independently trained template-ID probe accuracy.
Frozen gated TypeBind scored 83% triple-operator exact match, but an independently trained probe reached 36% template-ID accuracy.
Retain triple-operator gating for 83% exact match, but reject the invariance claim until the independent probe’s 36% accuracy is addressed.
Retain triple-operator gating; penalize probe-identified template leakage in slot embeddings, then retest ≥80% triple exact match and <30% independent-probe accuracy.
Fit leakage probes on gated TypeBind slot embeddings; penalize identified template directions and rerun five-seed triple-composition evaluations.
TypeBind-LeakGuard-v1: gated parser checkpoint, slot-embedding leakage penalty, five-seed evaluation outputs, and independent-probe training scripts.
Independently reproduce LeakGuard-v1’s five-seed TemplateFlip-v1 triple and in-distribution exact match; train fresh template-ID probes on frozen slot embeddings.
Independent LeakGuard-v1 replication found 81% triple-operator exact match, 29% fresh-probe template-ID accuracy, and a 1.5-point in-distribution deficit.
Advance LeakGuard-v1 to full-composition evaluation: independent probe falls from 36% to 29%, triple exact match 81%, in-distribution deficit 1.5 points.
Train WitnessRank with execution witnesses that distinguish operator-order program negatives, plus baseline-logit distillation for in-distribution accuracy.
How often can WitnessRank find a distinguishing execution witness for operator-order negatives in TemplateFlip-v1 triple compositions?
Bounded execution over 32 synthetic databases finds distinguishing witnesses for at least 90% of triple-operator order negatives.
Generate 1,000 TemplateFlip-v1 triple-operator order negatives; execute each pair against 32 seeded databases and measure witness coverage.
Across 1,000 triple-operator negatives, 32 seeded databases distinguished 927 pairs, yielding 92.7% execution-witness coverage.
Stratify WitnessRank's 1,000 triple-operator negatives by operator ordering; check witness coverage and semantic equivalence of unresolved pairs.
All 73 unresolved negatives were gold-equivalent but structurally distinct filter–count reorderings; execution witnesses cannot distinguish this exact-match class.
Retain witness ranking for 927 distinguishable pairs; handle 73 equivalent filter–count reorderings with gold-serialization supervision.
Can gold-serialization supervision resolve equivalent filter–count reorderings without reducing WitnessRank’s accuracy on distinguishable triple-operator pairs?
Gold-serialization supervision yields at least 80% exact match on equivalent filter–count reorderings without reducing distinguishable-pair accuracy by over one point.
Train WitnessRank with and without gold-serialization loss; measure exact match on 73 equivalent reorderings and accuracy on 927 distinguishable pairs.
Gold-serialization loss raised equivalent-reordering exact match from 64% to 85%; distinguishable-pair accuracy fell 0.4 points.
Adopt hybrid WitnessRank: serialize equivalent reorderings and rank distinguishable negatives by witnesses, accepting the 0.4-point pairwise accuracy cost.
Train hybrid WitnessRank; evaluate disjoint filter–count reorderings, distinguishable triple compositions, and in-distribution exact match against serialization-free controls.
Train five-seed hybrid and serialization-free WitnessRank models; score disjoint equivalent reorderings, distinguishable triples, and TemplateFlip-v1 in-distribution programs.
WitnessRank-Hybrid-v1: five-seed checkpoints, witness-pair training sets, serialization-loss ablations, and disjoint evaluation splits with exact-match scores.
Independently rerun WitnessRank-Hybrid-v1 on disjoint reorderings and distinguishable triples; compare in-distribution exact match with a same-size baseline.
Independent reruns found 82% exact match on disjoint equivalent reorderings, 81% on distinguishable triples, and a 1.7-point in-distribution deficit.
Advance WitnessRank alongside LeakGuard and audited swaps: witnesses handle 81% of distinguishable triples; serialization handles 82% of equivalents.
